t: From 1902 to 1934 the Platt Amendment, written into both Cuban and American law, gave the United States the right to intervene in Cuba, restricted its foreign relations and leased it the naval base at Guantánamo Bay.

Sugar ruled its politics: the First World War boom and the 1920 crash known as the Dance of the Millions ruined the country and handed more power to foreign investors, and by 1959 American firms owned about 40 per cent of the sugar land, 90 per cent of the mines and 80 per cent of the utilities.

The 1940 constitution wrote the right to work and to health care into law, but after his coup of 1952 Batista suspended it, and his secret police killed between hundreds and about 20,000 people before he fled in December 1958.
dyk: In 1950 Cuba became the first country in Latin America to broadcast television, and by the late 1950s it had the ninth highest number of television sets and the fourth highest number of channels of any country in the world.
ev: On 20 May Cuba gains formal independence as the Republic of Cuba, its constitution granting the United States the right to intervene under the Platt Amendment.
After a rigged election veterans rise in the August Revolution; President Tomás Estrada Palma resigns with his cabinet, and the United States occupies the island until 1909.
The Partido Independiente de Color's attempt to set up a separate Black republic in Oriente is crushed by the army under General Monteagudo with considerable bloodshed.
Sugar prices peak and crash in the Dance of the Millions, ruining the country financially and strengthening foreign investors.
A general strike, sugar workers' uprisings and an army revolt force Gerardo Machado into exile; in September the Sergeants' Revolt under Fulgencio Batista overthrows his successor.
The Treaty of Relations ends the Platt Amendment, binding Cuba to favour the American economy in return for a guaranteed 22 per cent of the U.S. sugar market.
A new constitution with the rights to labour and health care is adopted, and Batista is elected president.
Batista seizes power in a coup before the presidential election, suspends the 1940 constitution and revokes most political liberties.

f.founder: Tomás Estrada Palma, the first president, at formal independence on 20 May 1902
f.predecessor: The United States military government of Cuba, after Spain ceded the island by the Treaty of Paris of 1898
f.successor: Revolutionary Cuba, after Fulgencio Batista fled into exile in December 1958 and the Cuban Revolution triumphed in 1959
